NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATIONS. None of these changes my verdict; I am recording them so they are not rediscovered.

N1. THE `if not pr_number: return False` GUARD IS UNTESTED, AND NEARLY UNREACHABLE. Mutation probe: deleting it leaves 534/534 green. That is not a test gap so much as a behavioural near-identity -- with pr_number=0 the computed prefixes are 'reviews/0/' and 'proof/0.json', which match nothing in this repository, so the guard only changes the answer for a commit touching exactly those paths. It is correct and I would keep it; a single assertion that _is_record_only_commit(sha, 0) is False for a commit under reviews/45/ would pin the intent that the --pr-number help text states.

N2. A MAINTAINERS DOC NOW DESCRIBES THE OLD RULE. docs/maintainers/proof-of-completion-plan.md:678 says 'resolve_reviewable_head treats only `reviews/` and `proof/` as record-only'. After this PR it treats only `reviews/<pr>/` and `proof/<pr>.json`. The sentence's operative conclusion -- that a commit touching HANDOFF.md moves the reviewable head -- is unaffected, which is why I am not blocking on it, but the premise is now inexact and this repository holds itself to exactness about its own mechanisms. One sentence in a follow-up.
(Separately and NOT this PR's: docs/maintainers/session-protocol.md:141 calls a HANDOFF.md-only commit 'record-only, skipped when computing the review head'. That was false under the OLD rule too -- HANDOFF.md has never been record-only -- so it is pre-existing, and I checked before raising it.)

N3. THE EXEMPTION IS BY PATH, NOT BY FILENAME OR CONTENT. Any file under `reviews/<pr>/` rides it, not only a `*.json` record -- `_review_ok` globs `*.json`, but `_is_record_only_commit` does not care. Nothing in this repository executes content under reviews/, so the blast radius is small, and narrowing it further is a judgement call rather than a defect.

N4. THE RE-CUT CONVENTION CHANGES SHAPE, UNMENTIONED IN THE PR BODY. This repo's re-cut pattern renames `proof/<old>.json` -> `proof/<new>.json` in a commit of its own (#43 did it twice). Under the new rule that commit touches a path that is NOT `proof/<pr>.json`, so it is no longer record-only: it moves the reviewable head and loses the identity exemption. I think that is the RIGHT answer -- re-declaring a proof record is a content change -- but it is a workflow consequence worth writing down before it surprises the next re-cut. M5 shows it changes nothing for any PR open today.

N5. NOT THIS PR'S, CARRIED FORWARD FOR THE RECORD. `python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute` on this branch reports 'MISMATCH: 1' and EXIT 1 -- proof/39.json's `lwb_handoff.py --check` entry, recorded at 2961 bytes against this branch's HANDOFF.md. proof/README.md names 'a byte count' verbatim as disqualifying for verifiable:true, so proof/39.json (on main) breaks its own README's rule and every future PR that edits HANDOFF.md will report this. It is report-only today. I saw the identical mismatch reviewing #43. proof/45.json does NOT repeat the mistake.
